title: Hand Claude a folder, get back a lesson deck
learner: High school biology teacher. Unit notes, lab data and last year's slides live in one folder on their Mac.

steps.text: This is your Unit 3 folder: two weeks of notes, a reading, lab data and last unit's deck.
Give Claude the whole folder, not one file. It can read everything inside and save work back to it.
Describe the outcome you want, the way you'd brief a colleague.
Turn my Unit 3 notes into a 10-slide deck for Monday. Chart the osmosis lab results on one slide, and match the look of my Unit 2 deck.

items: Read both weeks of notes and the reading
Match the layout of Unit 2 – Genetics.pptx
Build 10 slides with speaker notes, save to this folder

steps.text: Claude shows its plan before it starts. You can redirect it here.
Then it works through your files.
The finished deck is saved back into your folder.

Your deck is saved in Unit 3 – Cells: 10 slides with speaker notes. Slide 6 charts the osmosis lab. Trial 4 gained mass in salt water, which doesn't fit the other five, so I flagged it on the slide instead of dropping it. Worth checking before Monday.
Claude flags what it isn't sure about. Deciding what's right is still your call.

slide.title: Osmosis lab: mass change in 5% salt water
slide.notes: Ask: why would a potato slice lose mass in salt water? What might explain trial 4?

steps.text: It's a normal file. Open it, check the flagged trial, edit what you'd teach differently.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pick one folder you'll work in this week. Give Claude the folder and an outcome, not a question.
steps.prompt: Using the files in this folder, make me ___ for ___. Flag anything you're unsure about.
